ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Wilma Mankiller Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient with six weeks of drooping eyelids, double vision and fatigable weakness while recovering from a car crash: examination, ice pack test, breathing measurements, baseline tests, a pyridostigmine trial, kidney screening, and neuromuscular neurology referral. Concerns: She wants to know why her eyelids droop and her arms give out, after a year of hard recovery; She wants to keep working for her community; She wants care that respects her as a Cherokee woman, close to home where possible, with her own medicine respected. [S]

tr.td: CT of the chest with contrast: residual thymic tissue appropriate for age, without a mass; no thymoma; healed rib fractures on the right; lungs clear

Ultrasound of the kidneys: both kidneys enlarged with many cysts (right 14.1 cm, left 14.6 cm); total kidney volume by the ellipsoid method 594 mL, height-adjusted 364 mL/m, Mayo Imaging Class 1B; several small liver cysts; no stones

Repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz with needle-free surface recording: reproducible decrement of 22 percent in the nasalis and 18 percent in the trapezius, with partial repair after exercise; normal sensory and motor conduction
Bedside measurement of breathing: negative inspiratory force -70 cm H2O, single-breath count to 32, with the seated FVC
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, with her consent
Robotic thoracoscopic extended thymectomy from the right, with two nights in hospital and no postoperative myasthenic worsening; pathology: thymic follicular hyperplasia, no thymoma

tr.td: New patient with six weeks of drooping eyelids, double vision and fatigable weakness while recovering from a car crash: examination, ice pack test, breathing measurements, baseline tests, a pyridostigmine trial, kidney screening, and neuromuscular neurology referral
Two-week review with the neuromuscular neurology consultation the same day: antibody, nerve stimulation, chest CT and kidney ultrasound results, the diagnosis, and the treatment plan
Six-week review on pyridostigmine and prednisone: strength, breathing, glucose and blood pressure, bone density, start of azathioprine, and the thymectomy plan
Review five weeks after thymectomy: recovery, pathology, azathioprine monitoring, the prednisone taper, and kidney care
Seven-month review: minimal manifestation status, prednisone and pyridostigmine reduction, azathioprine safety, kidney screening, and plans for the year

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Neuromuscular neurology consultation within two weeks for suspected generalized myasthenia gravis: diagnosis, immunotherapy, thymectomy and safety

Diagnostic tests: acetylcholine receptor binding antibodies (MuSK antibodies if negative), repetitive nerve stimulation (single-fiber EMG if unclear), CT of the chest with contrast for thymoma, TSH, and seated FVC with negative inspiratory force

Safety: pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily as a trial; warning signs of myasthenic crisis (breathlessness lying flat, weak cough, trouble swallowing, slurred speech) with emergency care the same day; a wallet card and the list of medicines to avoid, including fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides, magnesium by vein, beta-blockers and telithromycin

Kidney care for her hereditary polycystic kidney disease: kidney ultrasound with total kidney volume, eGFR and urine albumin, home blood pressure readings, 2 to 3 liters of water a day spread through the day, less salt, and acetaminophen instead of NSAIDs

Culturally safe care: laboratory work at a Cherokee Nation Health Services clinic near her home, results shared with this clinic; time given to explain each test and medicine plainly; her own Cherokee medicine respected, with any plant medicine shared so that interactions can be checked, and nothing further asked

Immunotherapy: pyridostigmine 60 mg four times daily; prednisone 10 mg each morning rising by 10 mg a week to 40 mg; azathioprine after TPMT activity and hepatitis B and tuberculosis screening, from 50 mg to 150 mg daily; pneumococcal and recombinant zoster vaccines before immunosuppression; no live vaccines
Thymectomy: thoracic surgery assessment for robotic extended thymectomy once she is stable, for AChR antibody-positive generalized MG at 34

Glucocorticoid safety: calcium and vitamin D, DXA within the first months, glucose and hemoglobin A1c, blood pressure and weight at each visit, sleep and mood, eye examination yearly, and Pneumocystis prophylaxis while prednisone is 20 mg or more with azathioprine
Azathioprine monitoring: blood count and liver tests every one to two weeks for the first two months, then every three months

Newer targeted therapies (efgartigimod, eculizumab or ravulizumab) kept in reserve for refractory disease or intolerance of standard immunotherapy; complement inhibitors would need meningococcal vaccination first
Standing laboratory orders at the Cherokee Nation Health Services clinic near her home for every azathioprine blood test, with results sent to this clinic and a nurse call for each result
A confirmed diagnosis and treatment plan within three weeks
AChR antibodies, nerve stimulation, chest CT and kidney ultrasound done; generalized MG diagnosed and treatment begun at two weeks
Minimal manifestation status (MG-ADL 0 to 1) within a year, with prednisone at 7.5 mg or less
MG-ADL 7 at diagnosis, 1 at seven months; prednisone 15 mg and still tapering
No myasthenic crisis, and she knows the warning signs and the medicines to avoid
No crisis; FVC 3.25 to 3.62 L; she carries a wallet card and the list of medicines to avoid
Kidney health: eGFR and urine albumin yearly, home blood pressure 110/75 mm Hg or lower if it rises above 130/85, 2 to 3 liters of water a day, and no NSAIDs
eGFR normal; urine albumin normal; home blood pressure about 116/74 without medicine
Return to full-time work for the Cherokee Nation
Back at work full time from the seventh month
